description: What the factory installs under a project and how a reinstall treats each path. Read by scripts/install_paths.py (classify, validate_table, scan_tree, moves, gitignore_block). Classes: carried = content only a person or a past run produced, kept; regenerated = a current script rebuilds it, never carried by hand; discarded = no current reader, offered for retirement; not_ours = recognised by name but never the factory's to change (an earlier generation's trace, or the project's own tooling such as its dev factory), never touched, never in a retire list. Precedence when a path matches several rules: carried, then regenerated, then discarded, then not_ours (fixed in code, not here). reader = a script name (resolved under scripts/), a package-relative path, or none; `none` is verified by a grep of the package. machine_local = differs per machine, carries no sha in the install manifest and is compared by name only in a tree comparison (its bytes are never looked at, its absence is named). retire_safe false = never put in a retire list by classification (locks). retire_mode = what a retirement does to an item, decided PER CLASS (owner, t-232 F2) and read from `retire_modes` below, never from code: delete for the factory's own technical data (every discarded row carries it, and so does a regenerated row whose `discard_when` proved it stale); move for anything undetermined; nothing for carried (a carried row never carries a retire_mode, validate_table refuses it). TWO FOLDERS (owner, t-232 F7+F8): `folders` names the two class folders of the factory's home, so it is visible at a glance what git ignores and what it does not - `records` is tracked and holds the carried records, `state` is machine-local and ignored whole. The `.gitignore` block is DERIVED from this table (one line per untracked folder, plus the `gitignore_block.inside_tracked` lines for generated files inside a tracked folder); validate_table refuses a carried non-machine-local row inside an untracked folder and a machine-local row inside a tracked one. A carried row with `moved_to` is the OLD place of a record an earlier factory kept there: a reinstall MOVES the file (bytes unchanged) to the new place, and until then the old place is read as a fallback (runtime_paths.py); the new place is the carried row whose glob equals `moved_to`. REGENERATED means a current script rebuilds the file: `regenerate_step` lists, per script the install's regenerate step runs, the files it writes (`outputs`); a regenerated file that is NOT among the outputs of this run is a leftover nothing rebuilds and is retired (deleted, listed by name) under the person's one word, while a carried path is never retired whatever regenerated row also matches it (precedence). `lock_kind` marks a lock row (always `retire_safe: false`): `os` = an OS lock on a file, provably stale when nobody holds it, removed by the install only when the row is regenerated; `exclusive_create` = the file's existence is the lock (O_EXCL); `folder` = a folder made with mkdir is the lock; the last two are listed when older than a day and never removed, and so is any lock under a carried row. `hook_written: true` (regenerated rows only, never with retire_mode or discard_when, never on a glob that covers a regenerate_step output) = rewritten by a running session's hooks; never retired, never in the sealed listing, never in the manifest; its stale OS locks are neither removed nor counted; compared by name only.

an OS byte-range lock on the file (event_store.take_file_lock): exit_gate.py runs inside hooks and opens it at every state update, so it is hook-written; a leftover of a killed hook is free at once and the file is never deleted

explore_step.py makes it with O_CREAT|O_EXCL: its existence IS the lock of one exploration (state/ is not committed, so a crashed session's lock never reaches git). Listed when older than a day, never removed; `explore_step.py release` is the door. Stands ABOVE the generic state/**/*.lock row (the first row of a kind that names a lock wins)
older generation; never made by this version; listed, never removed
hook-written (the pre-tool guard records findings through it via add_finding): an OS byte-range lock on the file (event_store.take_file_lock); a leftover is free at once and the file is never deleted

an OS byte-range lock on the file: when nobody holds it a leftover is provably stale and the install removes it; a held one refuses the install. A lock under a carried row (cost/.writers/**) is listed by name and never removed
a copy a killed probe left; recovery reads it
a lease registry: a lease whose holder is alive refuses the install (find_locks); with none alive the file is a leftover this install does not rebuild. Its .lock file is the lock row above
the conductor wake's fuse (HF8-15 (1b)): a running session's Stop hook rewrites it; losing it costs one extra wake

hooklib journals from the hooks of every running session through log_append, so the writer's lock is made again at each tool call (t-363 B6: a lock is 1 byte, no session id or pid inside); same class as .dashboard-writer

the event store's lock, taken by hooklib from the hooks of a running session (t-363 B6); the generic state/**/*.lock row still classifies it, this row only marks it hook-written. A stray lock under any other name stays counted
the writer lock of the stand registry; named so the `stand-*.json` row (stand_lease) never claims it
the report a probe run wrote and the code could not read, with its manifest (B-416): the folder of a profile is replaced by the next unread run
state/budget/<task>.json: project state, disposable (story_budget.py)

a probe cache: the doctor and the onboarding rewrite it on every run, so it stays in state/ and never moves. The one thing a reinstall keeps of it is the person's own answer, which tracker_write.py --record also writes as a `tracker_write_answer` line into records/onboarding-approvals.jsonl
